description:
Bravú asserted a modern Galician cultural identity by melding the old and the new, the rural and the urban, into a hybrid culture described as "rurban" and "glocal." This philosophy was accompanied by a distinctive raw and defiant visual aesthetic that incorporated Galician cultural symbols into a DIY, punk-inspired graphic style. The movement was officially named in 1994. [ 1 ]
